issues.description: The script fetches and executes remote JavaScript code from https://deadshot-cheat.netlify.app/index.js at runtime using eval(). This is a critical remote code execution risk, as the remote code can be changed at any time and executed with full user privileges.
issues.recommendation: Avoid dynamic code execution from remote sources. Bundle all code with the script and avoid eval(). If remote code is necessary, use integrity checks and fixed versions.

issues.description: The script uses eval() to execute arbitrary code loaded from a remote server. This is a high-severity security risk.
issues.recommendation: Do not use eval() on untrusted or remote code. Refactor to avoid eval() entirely.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest and unsafeWindow permissions, which are high-privilege and can be abused if the script or remote code is compromised.
issues.recommendation: Minimize permissions to only those required. Avoid unsafeWindow and GM_xmlhttpRequest unless absolutely necessary.

issues.description: The script loads remote code from a non-official domain (deadshot-cheat.netlify.app) without version pinning or integrity verification, introducing supply chain risk.
issues.recommendation: Only load code from trusted, official sources with version pinning and integrity checks.

summary: This UserScript presents a critical security risk. It dynamically fetches and executes remote JavaScript code using eval(), granting the remote server full control over the user's browser context. This exposes users to arbitrary code execution, data theft, and other severe threats. The use of high-privilege permissions and unpinned remote code further increases the risk. This script should NOT be approved or used in any secure environment.
